articles.title: In 2020, an Idaho condominium association changed owners' common-property shares and rental and boat-mooring rules; an October 30 Supreme Court ruling revived a challenge to the ownership allocations despite an 88% vote
articles.summary: The Idaho Supreme Court has brought a legal challenge by condominium owners back to life over disputed changes to shared property ownership.
articles.body: The Idaho Supreme Court has brought a legal challenge by condominium owners back to life over disputed changes to shared property ownership. The court ruled that even a large majority vote cannot override laws that protect individual property rights. According to legal documents published by Justia Law, the state's highest court issued its ruling on 30 October in K & L Crystal Beach, LLC v. The Crystal Beach Condominium Association (Docket No. 52887). The decision partly overturned an earlier ruling by a lower court in Valley County. It allows condominium owners K & L Crystal Beach, LLC and Kathleen Glover to continue their legal claims against changes made to the property's official declaration by their association. The dispute began after a 2020 vote in which the Crystal Beach Condominium Association recorded an amended declaration. The changes affected owners' property shares, rental rules and access to boat moorings across the development.Supermajority vote altered long-standing property allocationsUnder the original 1965 declaration for the Crystal Beach development, each condominium unit had a fixed percentage of ownership in the shared areas. Every unit was given a 1.595 per cent share of the common property, along with matching voting rights. In 2020, the association approved changes to the declaration with the support of 88 per cent of its members. The new rules changed how ownership shares in the common areas were divided among unit owners. They also introduced new rules for rental activities and access to boat slips within the shared areas. After the updated declaration was officially recorded, K & L Crystal Beach and condominium owner Kathleen Glover filed a lawsuit to challenge the changes. They argued that changing ownership percentages without getting approval from every owner broke the Condominium Property Act. They also claimed that the changes unfairly reduced their legal property rights.Lower court dismissal reversed on core ownership claimsA judge at the Fourth Judicial District Court in Valley County had earlier ruled in favour of the condominium association through summary judgment. The trial court decided that the plaintiffs did not have the legal right to bring several of their claims. It treated the case as a dispute brought on behalf of the association and its members under the Idaho Nonprofit Corporation Act, rather than as a direct case involving the owners' personal property rights. After reviewing the case, the Idaho Supreme Court overturned part of that decision. The justices found that claims challenging changes to individual ownership shares in common areas involve direct harm to personal property rights. They are not simply disputes about how a company or association is run. The court explained that association rules covering general operations, short-term rentals and boat-mooring access apply equally to members and are generally covered by company governance rules. However, changes that directly affect an owner's percentage of legal property ownership must strictly follow the laws governing property rights.Case remanded for further proceedings in Valley CountyThe ruling keeps the lower court's decision on general association rules, including shared mooring arrangements and rental restrictions. The Supreme Court agreed that these matters were related to the association's overall management and should be treated as group claims. However, by overturning the dismissal of the main ownership claims, the high court has allowed the plaintiffs to continue their direct legal claims. These include requests for declaratory relief, quiet title and slander of title. The case now returns to the District Court of the Fourth Judicial District in Valley County. The lower court will continue examining whether the changes to ownership shares approved in 2020 followed the legal requirements for condominium property declarations.You use AI every day. articles.title: An 82-year-old Florida man has spent seven decades collecting magazines, photographs and celebrity memorabilia; his one-man museum now includes a thank-you letter from Elizabeth Taylor
articles.summary: Others preserve old photos because they are sentimental. Others save a magazine because it reminds them of a certain time.
articles.body: Others preserve old photos because they are sentimental. Others save a magazine because it reminds them of a certain time. But for Rudy Scaglione, collecting is a lifelong pursuit, a personal archive of seven decades of pop culture, Hollywood history and major world events. The Tampa resident, now 82, has amassed so many souvenirs he basically has built himself a museum.A collection covering seven decadesAccording to BayNews9, Scaglione started collecting as a teenager, saving magazines, newspapers, photographs and other bits of memorabilia. What started as a hobby never really ended, and his collection has continued to grow through the years.The archive now features some of the most memorable moments in modern American history, including the assassination of President John F. Kennedy, the September 11 attacks, the first moon landing and the civil rights movement, BayNews9 reports.Hollywood also takes up a substantial portion of his collection. Among his prized possessions are photographs and memorabilia associated with some of the industry’s best known stars, especially Elizabeth Taylor and Marilyn Monroe.A personal museum for fellow citizensThe exclusive report by BayNews9 states that his collection was kept for years in plastic tubs and bookcases at his assisted living home. He recently decided it was time to bring some of that out into the open.The result was a pop culture exhibition at Brookdale Bayshore in Tampa, where tables groaning with photographs, publications and celebrity memorabilia turned the facility’s lobby into a walk through decades of history, the report adds.Millie Post helped Scaglione organize and display the pieces as fellow residents got to check out the collection, BayNews9 reports. The exhibition also evoked memories for many of photographs and publications they once owned but have since thrown away.For Scaglione, wading through the material has been a reminder of the amount of history he’s witnessed in his lifetime.A Hollywood tie to holdOf the thousands of items he has collected, one has special sentimental value: a thank-you note from Elizabeth Taylor, explains the online report.Scaglione sent flowers and a get-well card to the Hollywood actress while she was in hospital. Her response became one of his most treasured possessions, adding a special touch to his already vast collection from one of the legends of the cinema world.BayNews9 reports the rest of the archive has been collected over years of buying from newsstands, subscriptions to newspapers and magazines and online purchases.What started with a teenager collecting things he found interesting has become an amazing record of changing times. By sharing his collection with fellow residents, Scaglione has found a way to make those memories part of other people’s lives, too.Images Courtesy: istock, Wikipedia, and BayNews9You use AI every day. articles.title: A professor at Rice University started an open-learning project in 1999; its free textbooks are now used by millions of students
articles.summary: A project started by a Rice University professor in 1999 has grown into an international effort to make education more accessible through free textbooks
articles.body: A project started by a Rice University professor in 1999 has grown into an international effort to make education more accessible through free textbooks and digital learning resources. Richard G. Baraniuk founded Connexions with the aim of making educational materials available online without the high costs traditionally associated with textbooks. More than two decades later, the initiative has evolved into OpenStax, a nonprofit educational project whose textbooks are used by millions of students across the world, helping reduce the financial burden of education.The Rice University professor began the open-learning projectThe story began in 1999, when Richard G. Baraniuk, a professor at Rice University in Houston, Texas, established Connexions, an online platform for sharing educational materials. According to Rice University, Baraniuk founded the project to bring textbooks and other learning resources into the internet age.At the time, traditional college textbooks could cost hundreds of dollars, creating an additional expense for students already dealing with tuition fees and other educational costs. The OpenStax website traces its origins to this problem, explaining that its founder wanted to create an alternative in which course materials could be developed and shared by the communities that used them.Rather than following the conventional publishing model, Connexions allowed educators, authors and learners to publish, modify and use educational content freely. The platform encouraged collaboration and gave teachers greater flexibility to adapt learning materials to their requirements.The project also attracted considerable attention in its early years. Connexions had become one of the largest open-education platforms, offering more than 19,000 educational modules and reaching over two million people each month.The transition from Connexions to OpenStax expanded the initiativeThe next major development came in 2012, when the original project evolved into OpenStax College, later known simply as OpenStax. The organisation moved beyond providing a platform for sharing educational material and began publishing complete, free textbooks for widely taught college subjects.OpenStax College planned to release free, publisher-quality textbooks for 5 of the most popular college courses in the United States.Its first two books, College Physics and Introduction to Sociology, were scheduled for publication in March that year. Three additional textbooks covering biology, anatomy and physiology were also in development.The initiative received financial backing from several organisations, including the William and Flora Hewlett Foundation, the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation, the 20 Million Minds Foundation and the Maxfield Foundation.The original plan focused on courses with large student enrolments, where expensive textbooks affected the greatest number of learners. Baraniuk estimated that reaching just 10% of the market with the first 5 books could help one million American college students save $90 million over five years.An important part of the model was that the books would not simply be free to read. Their open licences would also allow teachers to modify and adapt the content to suit their courses. Students could access the material through computers, tablets and smartphones, while affordable printed editions were available through print-on-demand services.What made the free textbook model differentOpenStax developed its publishing approach around two important principles, accessibility and academic quality. Unlike informal collections of online notes, its textbooks were designed to meet the standards expected of conventional academic publications.According to the organisation, its books are peer-reviewed and developed with contributions from educators working at community colleges, public universities, land-grant institutions and research universities.This approach allows students to access structured learning material without having to purchase expensive commercial textbooks. Teachers also benefit because openly licensed content can be adjusted to meet the needs of different classrooms and courses.The model has also expanded beyond simply providing digital books. OpenStax now develops additional learning tools, including Assignable, a practice and assessment system designed to support teaching and help students understand course material.Its work also includes education research through SafeInsights, a Rice University initiative that studies how students learn and how educational resources can be improved.OpenStax marked a decade with 50 textbook titlesBy 2022, the initiative had reached an important milestone. In a March 31, 2022, report titled 10 for 10, Rice University News marked OpenStax's 10th anniversary of publishing free textbooks.The organisation announced plans to release 10 new titles during that year, expanding its collection for students and educators. Two of the latest publications mentioned in the report were Introduction to Anthropology and the Writing Guide with Handbook, designed for English composition courses.These additions brought the total number of available textbooks to 50 at the time. Further titles were also being developed in subjects such as finance, political science, computer applications, contemporary mathematics and world history.The report highlighted how far the initiative had progressed since publishing its first textbook in 2012. OpenStax has partnered with more than 60 educational technology providers to help educators use its resources across different disciplines.It had also saved more than 22 million students an estimated $1.7 billion through its open educational resources, according to the 2022 report.Millions of students now benefit from the initiativeOpenStax's reach has continued to grow beyond its original focus on American college courses. The organisation has reached 49 million students in total, with 5.4 million students reached annually.The students have saved $3.8 billion through its resources over time, including $374.3 million in annual savings. Its materials have reached learners across 172 countries, while 71% of US colleges and universities use its resources annually.The organisation also reports that its materials are used by 56,810 educators and 9,710 K-12 schools each year. Its digital resources attract approximately 15 million active web users annually.OpenStax has also extended its reach through translations and partnerships. Availability of textbooks in multiple languages, including Spanish. A Polish nonprofit partner, OpenStax Polska, has adapted its educational titles for local students, with its physics edition accounting for 70% of the Polish market.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 1964, an Edinburgh antiques dealer paid just £5 for a small carved warrior; after spending decades in a family drawer, it was identified as a missing Lewis chess piece and sold for £735,000
articles.summary: A small carved ivory figure bought for just £5 by an Edinburgh antiques dealer in 1964 has sold at auction for £735,000 after experts identified it as a
articles.body: A small carved ivory figure bought for just £5 by an Edinburgh antiques dealer in 1964 has sold at auction for £735,000 after experts identified it as a long-lost Lewis chessman. The sale set an official record for the most expensive medieval chess piece ever sold at auction, according to Guinness World Records. The 8.8-centimetre figure is made from walrus tusk and represents a warder, which is the equivalent of a rook in modern chess. For 55 years, the chess piece was kept inside a drawer at the home of the dealer's daughter. She had no idea about its historical importance or how much it could be worth.Decades in a family drawerThe story of the missing warder began in 1964, when an Edinburgh antiques dealer bought the small ivory figure from another local dealer. He recorded the purchase in his sales book as an "Antique Walrus Tusk Warrior Chessman". After his death, his daughter inherited the figure. A family spokesperson told Sotheby's that although the family did not know exactly what the object was, its owner loved it because of its unusual appearance. "My mother was very fond of the Chessman as she admired its intricacy and quirkiness," the spokesperson said in a statement released through the auction house. "She believed that it was special and thought perhaps it could even have had some magical significance. For many years it resided in a drawer in her home where it had been carefully wrapped in a small bag." The family eventually took the figure to Sotheby's in London for a free valuation. Experts quickly recognised that it was a genuine Lewis chessman.Expert identification at Sotheby'sAlexander Kader, Sotheby's co-worldwide head of European sculpture and works of art, recalled when the family first brought the figure in for an assessment. "They brought it in for assessment. That happens everyday. Our doors are open for free valuations," Kader told the Press Association. "We get called down to the counter and have no idea what we are going to see. More often than not, it's not worth very much. I said, 'Oh my goodness, it's one of the Lewis Chessmen.'" Kader kept the discovery secret for six months while experts carried out checks to confirm its identity. He described the warder as having a weathered appearance and said its worn condition added to its historical charm. "When you hold this characterful warder in your hand or see him in the room, he has real presence," Kader told The Guardian. "This is one of the most exciting and personal rediscoveries to have been made during my career."Significance of the Lewis hoardThe newly identified figure is part of the famous Lewis Chessmen collection. The original hoard contains 93 carved objects and was discovered in 1831 among the sand dunes of Uig on the Isle of Lewis in the Outer Hebrides. Historians believe the pieces were made in Norway between 1150 and 1200 AD. Most of the collection, including 82 pieces, is kept at the British Museum in London. Another 11 pieces are held at the National Museum of Scotland in Edinburgh. Before this discovery, five pieces from the original collection were believed to be missing. These included one knight and four warders. With the sale of the newly identified warder at Sotheby's, four pieces are still missing. Kader said finding the remaining pieces could take many generations. "There are still four out there somewhere," he said. "It might take another 150 years for another one to pop up."You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Sherlock Holmes creator Arthur Conan Doyle's 14-bedroom UK mansion fell into ruin after 2004; a £7.5 million rescue turned the abandoned house into a school
articles.summary: Explore the transformation of Sir Arthur Conan Doyle's Undershaw mansion, once abandoned and decaying, into a thriving school for disabled children after a significant £7.5 million rescue initiative. Discover its rich literary history and the efforts made to preserve this historic property.
articles.body: A house associated with one of, if not the best, fiction writers in literature went through a period of uncertainty after its life as a hotel ended. Sir Arthur Conan Doyle’s Victorian residence in Hindhead, Surrey, called Undershaw, was left in complete neglect after 2004. A proposed conversion into separate dwellings prompted a legal challenge, and the building eventually found a new purpose as a school for disabled children. According to the Conan Doyle Estate, the work followed a £7.5 million fundraising effort, and the former residence became the home of Stepping Stones School, which had previously operated from a nearby church.A threatened heritage property Conan moved into Undershaw in 1897 and stayed there until 1907, the estate reported. The house was designed to his own specifications, ensuring it accommodated the family’s needs. The residence is anchored by a deep literary legacy, as it was the place where Conan penned the classic work The Hound of the Baskervilles. On top of that, it also served as a host to other great writers, J. M. Barrie and Bram Stoker, whose works included Peter and Wendy and Dracula, respectively.Subsequently, the property changed hands following Conan Doyle’s departure; it was rented out and eventually sold in 1920. After he died in 1930, the historic significance of the building survived and by 1924, it was converted into a hotel and remained so until 2004.The closure left the property vulnerable. The Conan Doyle Estate’s account states that it underwent extensive deterioration, with windows damaged and a roof through which daylight leaked. The building’s condition became a central concern as proposals emerged to redevelop it for housing.The New York Times reported in 2012 that the redevelopment approval had been overturned by the High Court. If the plan had gone through, then it would have divided Undershaw into three separate buildings and an additional five more. The legal challenge was brought by supporters who sought to protect the building, including the Undershaw Preservation Trust.The same report highlights the court’s decision to quash the redevelopment plans on the grounds that the owners had not properly consulted English Heritage, the organisation in charge of historic buildings. The ruling prevented the approved scheme from proceeding as planned, but it did not settle the property’s long-term future. A borough council lawyer, Bryn Morgan, was wary of the decision and said, “Sadly, the decision by the High Court places the future of the building back in doubt once again. The poor condition of the building will now only get worse.”The dispute received much media spotlight and brought support from literary and cultural figures alike, including Julian Barnes, Ian Rankin, Stephen Fry, Benedict Cumberbatch and Mark Gatiss.Restoration of the past and educating the future The next decisive change came in 2014, when David Fiorbes-Nixon purchased Undershaw through the DFM Foundation. Nixon’s son at the time attended Stepping Stones, a nearby school that would eventually occupy the property. According to the Guardian report on 3 April 2014, the purchase concluded a near-decade-long preservation campaign. Stepping Stones offered a practical future for a building whose large rooms could be modified for teaching. The fact that a literary giant’s residence was being turned into a school was very fitting and allowed it to remain in use, rather than being divided into residential units.In the Conan Doyle Estate’s 2017 account, Stepping Stones business Anne Edward explained that much of the original interior was left intact during restoration, including its fireplaces. There was, however, an extension that was done, which provided extra space and reduced the need to alter the building itself.The changes were limited; as per Edward’s account, one wall was removed to connect the extension of the house, while an internal wall was changed. Conan Doyle's former study, where he wrote The Hound of the Baskervilles, became the headteacher's office. His wife's room, noted for its bay windows and views, became the school library. Following the estate’s report, the restored property was nominated for a Surrey Heritage Award, and the winner was announced on 12 April 2017.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Golden Triangle's North East drug trade thrives on barter
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: International illicit drug syndicates operating out of the Golden Triangle of Myanmar, Thailand and Laos have turned to age-old barter trade,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: International illicit drug syndicates operating out of the Golden Triangle of Myanmar, Thailand and Laos have turned to age-old barter trade, under which drugs like heroin and methamphetamine are smuggled into India through the porous borders of Northeastern states and payments are made in kind through supplies of petrol, diesel, flour, edible oil, groceries, medicines, footwear and clothing from their Indian network.Drug lords across border ensure transactions are made without any money actually crossing border, according to an investigation report compiled by the ED after week-long searches at 38 locations across the Northeast last week.Myanmar has already replaced Afghanistan as world's largest illicit opium-producing region. With precursor chemicals moved from India to Myanmar, where drug manufacturing units are located, finished heroin, brown sugar and synthetic drug methamphetamine tablets are produced and carried across the Tiau river at Zokhawthar, the border crossing opposite Khawmawi in Myanmar. Consignments are staged at Champhai, from where they travel down the Champhai-Aizawl road and NH-06A to Aizawl, Vairengte and then to Assam and the rest of India, the ED report said.ED has traced intermediaries who procured and supplied goods to syndicates in Myanmar. Over 1,400 mule bank accounts, mostly belonging to traders who procured these goods and supplied them to the network, have been frozen. Transactions involving goods worth over Rs 270 crore have been identified so far and six persons arrested. These transactions were handled by illicit money exchangers, or hawala networks, in Champhai, including Rs 125 crore in cash received from Assam, Nagaland, WB, Tripura & Delhi, ED said.Significantly, drug money reaching hawala accounts in Aizawl and Champhai came substantially from Delhi, Kolkata and Mumbai, ED added. Illegal money is converted into ordinary, commercially marketable goods, which are sent to border towns of Mizoram and onward to Myanmar."The banking system is thus used only for Indian leg of the transaction, where the payment looks like an ordinary trade payment backed by a GST invoice. The cross-border leg moves as goods and leaves no money trail. In effect, fuel, flour and groceries have become currency in which Myanmar-based drug suppliers are paid," ED said.The probe is in progress to identify consignees in border towns, those who move goods across border, Myanmar-based recipients, petrol pumps, shops and suppliers paid in the same manner, and money exchangers directing the accounts. ED is also tracing and attaching further proceeds of crime as it works to dismantle the financial networks sustaining narcotics trafficking.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Chewing-gum heir William Wrigley Jr. bought two Florida properties for $17.1 million in 2009 and 2010, built two mansions and sold them together for $97.5 million
articles.summary: William Wrigley Jr., the heir to the chewing-gum fortune, broke sales records in Lost Tree Village with the off-market sale of his North Palm Beach compound that he purchased for $17.1 million, transforming it into a $97.5 million estate.
articles.body: William Wrigley Jr. turned two North Palm Beach properties, which he purchased for a total sum of $17.1 million, and merged them into a compound that broke the Lost Tree Village sales record in 2025. According to The Wall Street Journal, the heir to the Wrigley gum fortune then sold the adjoining holdings in December 2025 for $97.5 million, yielding a price almost six times higher than their combined acquisition cost. The off-market transaction involved two properties at 11465 and 11472 Old Harbour Road, covering 2.5 acres within the private and gated community.Two properties acquired a year apartProperty records show that Wrigley had acquired the larger parcel for $11 million in 2009. The following year in 2010, the smaller adjoining property was purchased for $6.1 million, bringing his total cash outlay on the two holdings to $17.1 million. The two holdings consisted of separate parcels, each with a mansion, and those mansions were built in 2013 and 2014. The estate also has multiple docks and occupies a strip along the Intracoastal Waterway.The larger parcel includes undeveloped land adjacent to the principal residence, but the potential for developing that additional land remained unclear. On top of that, the properties were not listed publicly at the time of transaction, leaving limited information about the marketing process or the buyer’s plans. Wrigley was represented by Gary Pohrer of Serhant; conversely, the purchaser was represented by Douglas Elliman.Local agents, in their account to The Wall Street Journal, said the sale price was high for a property without ocean frontage. The transaction followed a $55 million Lost Tree Village sale in May 2025, which had an oceanfront residence, according to The Real Deal.The previous sales record of Lost Tree VillageThe earlier record-holding title belonged to Canadian baby-products entrepreneur Maurice Pinsonnault, who sold his property at 12032 East End for $55 million in May 2025. The purchaser of that property was also undisclosed.Lost Tree Village stretches over approximately 450 acres and accommodates more than 500 residences in its vicinity. It has an 18-hole golf course, which was designed by Jack Nicklaus, who’s considered to be one of the most prolific golf course architects.Wrigley’s financial history extends beyond the property market. He assumed control of the family business in 1999, before selling the Wrigley Company in 2008 to Mars Inc. for $23 billion in cash. Subsequently, he worked in the capacity of chief executive of the cannabis company Parallel in 2018. His financial footprint, as per Forbes, is estimated at $3.6 billion. Although the buyer was not disclosed at first, The Real Deal identified fintech billionaire Ronald Clarke as the buyer.Wrigley’s other transaction portfolio includes an Aspen, Colorado, mansion, which he sold for $30 million in 2022, as per the Wall Street Journal. The North Palm Beach transaction also falls below the highest residential sale reported in South Florida as of 2025. William Lauder sold two properties at 1063 and 1071 North Ocean Boulevard in Palm Beach, covering 2.3 acres, for more than $160 million earlier that year, according to The Real Deal.You use AI every day. articles.title: A 12-year-old boy from south London has raised more than £13,000 for endangered wildlife, built a 35,000-strong online following and caught David Attenborough's attention through his animal videos and campaigns
articles.summary: Most young children are still trying to figure out what they like. Not Leo Sordello-Savala.
articles.body: Most young children are still trying to figure out what they like. Not Leo Sordello-Savala. He’s already started his own conservation movement with his love of animals. The 12-year-old from Camberwell, south London has spent much of his childhood trying to make a difference from making videos about endangered species to organizing school fundraisers and supporting rewilding projects, reports London Post and Southwark News online. Now his work is said to have won him national recognition and a rare endorsement from one of Britain's most decorated naturalists, Sir David Attenborough. Scroll down to read more.From lockdown hobby to callIt was seven years ago that Leo’s journey began, with a simple idea of connecting with other young animal lovers and doing something meaningful about wildlife conservation, online reports say. It started as a personal project, and eventually became Leo’s Animal Planet, which spans YouTube, podcasts and other social media platforms.His online following has grown to more than 35,000 followers on several platforms, where he shares animal facts, educational videos and information on endangered species, according to the London Post. His content is said to seek to make wildlife conservation accessible to young people and inspire people to think differently about their relationship with the natural world, online reports say.£13,000+ for wild lifeA fundraising drive has also raised over £13,000 for animal charities and rewilding projects, fueling the growing online following, it is reported.London Post says he has discovered ways to help the causes he believes in. According to the report, he has donated profits from his online content, profits from a sustainable clothing shop hosted on Teemill and prize money from awards such as the 2025 London Eco Champion Award.His fundraising has also gone beyond the Internet. He has sold old toys, books and clothes and held school events with cakes and badges and participated in races to raise money for conservation. He has also worked with the Cheetah Conservation Fund, the Captain Paul Watson Foundation UK and Born Free where he is a young ambassador.A young activist with bigger ambitionsLeo was presented with the BCyA Medal of Honor at the Palace of Westminster on 29th October, alongside other young people from around the country who had been recognized for their achievements.It’s a big award for the young conservationist – but he’s not done yet. With a growing digital community, more partnerships and thousands of pounds already raised, Leo is continuing to use his platform to raise awareness of species and habitats that need protecting.It’s a reminder that conservation doesn’t have to start off with a big organization or a formal campaign. Sometimes it starts with a child, a camera and a genuine interest in the wildlife around us.Recognition from a conservation iconIn 2021, Sir David Attenborough sent one of the biggest moments of Leo’s journey: a handwritten letter acknowledging his work to protect wildlife. The award was a boost for the young campaigner, whose work began as a way of finding a community of like-minded animal lovers.Now Leo’s efforts have earned him a British Citizen Youth Award which celebrates young people who make a positive contribution to their communities and wider society, says Southwark News.Images Courtesy: London Post and WikipediaYou use AI every day. articles.title: A Texas couple bought an Austin house for $367,000 using funds the husband called gifts from his father and a friend; after the home was appraised at $646,192, an appeals court upheld the disputed divorce property split
articles.summary: A Texas appeals court has upheld a trial court's decision to divide property in a contested divorce.
articles.body: A Texas appeals court has upheld a trial court's decision to divide property in a contested divorce. The court ruled that the former husband failed to provide enough clear and convincing evidence to prove that an Austin home, bought for $367,000, belonged to him alone rather than being shared marital property. According to court records published by Justia Law, the Texas Twelfth Court of Appeals issued its decision in case number 12-26-00167-CV, upholding the final divorce ruling. The main issue was whether the former family home in Austin, later valued at $646,192, belonged to the couple jointly or was the husband's separate property. The appeals court found that the trial judge acted within the law when dividing the couple's property. The husband had failed to provide enough financial records to prove that money given to him as gifts was used to buy the home.Allegations of family gifts and unverified financial tracingDuring the trial, the husband said the original $367,000 purchase price of the Austin home was paid using money given to him separately by his father and a close personal friend. Under Texas family law, gifts received by one spouse during a marriage can be treated as that person's separate property. However, the person making this claim must provide strong evidence to support it. Texas law assumes that property owned or held by either spouse during a marriage, or when the marriage ends, belongs to both spouses. To challenge this rule, a person must provide clear and convincing evidence. This means the evidence must be strong enough to give the judge a firm belief that the claims being made are true. Court records show that the husband gave spoken testimony about the money received from his father and friend. However, he did not provide complete bank statements or other financial records showing exactly how the money moved into the property's closing escrow account. Without clear documents showing where the money came from and how it was used, the trial court treated the home as shared marital property that could be divided between the spouses.Significant appreciation increases stakes in property divisionThe value of the Austin home became an important issue during the divorce after property appraisals placed its market value at $646,192. The increase in value created a large amount of equity in the marital estate. Since the court classified the home as shared property, the trial judge ordered that the net equity be divided between both spouses as part of the overall division of their marital assets. The husband challenged the decision in the appeals court. He argued that the trial judge had made a mistake by treating his separate property as shared marital property and dividing the home's equity between the two sides.Appellate ruling confirms trial court discretionWhen reviewing the appeal, the Twelfth Court of Appeals considered whether the trial judge had enough evidence to decide how the property should be classified and divided. In its decision, the appeals court repeated that Texas trial judges have wide authority to divide shared marital property during a divorce. The division must be fair and reasonable, while taking the rights of both spouses into account. An appeals court will only overturn a property division if the person challenging it can show that the trial judge clearly abused this authority and that the mistake affected the fairness of the final division. The appeals court concluded that the husband had failed to meet Texas law's strict requirements for proving where the money used to buy the home came from. As a result, the trial judge was right to treat the Austin property as shared marital property. The Twelfth Court of Appeals upheld the trial court's full judgment. This means the original property division and the decision to share the home's equity between the former spouses remain unchanged.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: NEW DELHI: In a Ramlila Maidan packed with protesters and ringing with anti-BJP and anti-CEC slogans Sunday, Congress MP Rahul Gandhi said the opposition
articles.body: NEW DELHI: In a Ramlila Maidan packed with protesters and ringing with anti-BJP and anti-CEC slogans Sunday, Congress MP Rahul Gandhi said the opposition will confront the top BJP duo of Narendra Modi and Amit Shah after Gyanesh Kumar's removal as chief election commissioner. The trio was losing sleep over the agitation, he claimed, and said the CEC's exit would be the first step in putting the country back on track.With opposition biggies Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge, Sonia Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav, Mamata Banerjee, Tejashwi Yadav, Dipankar Bhattacharya, MA Baby, Farooq Abdullah and Mehbooba Mufti on the dais, leader of opposition in Lok Sabha said the "voice of the people of India" is greater to him than religion, and he will brook no assault on it.Mocking BJP's catchphrase - "Modi kahin nahin jayega" - which was coined in response to Kharge's comment, Rahul said the PM won't be allowed to go anywhere. "You cannot flee... You will stay here and face action."2024 polls illegal, says Rahul; Modi picking voters: KhargeWith a “vote bachao, desh bachao” banner forming the backdrop of the dais, the speakers focused on “vote chori”, repeating allegations about SIR and deletion of around 14 crore voters. Rahul accused the CEC, PM and Shah of suppressing the voice of people through “vote chori”. While Mamata and Akhilesh said the West Bengal mandate to BJP was “stolen”, Rahul mentioned the Maharashtra, Haryana, Chhattisgarh, MP and 2024 Lok Sabha polls.He said the 2024 polls were illegal, arguing the difference between NDA and opposition was merely 3%, while 15% of the 2024 voters have been deleted under SIR. “Modi is selecting the voters,” Congress chief Kharge said.Led by Kharge, most INDIA bloc members stressed ejecting BJP from office was a must to save democracy, even leading the crowd in “BJP hatao, desh bachao” chants.Some reminded the crowd that Ramlila Maidan has been the harbinger of history and change in the past. SP chief Akhilesh called the historic venue the “Haldighati of democracy”, referring to the battlefield in Rajasthan where Maharana Pratap faced off with the Mughals in 1576, remembered as a symbol of defiant resistance to a powerful empire.Addressing the crowd that had been growing since 9am and remained eager even as main INDIA bloc members came on the dais only by 3pm, Akhilesh, who occupied a key spot with UP polls looming, hit out at Modi, saying, “Jo UP se aaye the, woh UP se hi jaayenge (those who came from UP, will go from UP)”.“The UP poll results will see off BJP from office in Lucknow and Delhi,” he said, also raising “chanda chori” in Ayodhya in his speech. Akhilesh warned BJP was constantly trying to steal elections, even blaming SP’s 2022 assembly defeat on voter list manipulation. The SP chief said UP BJP has stated that 1.27 crore votes of Hindus have been deleted in UP. He said the statement seems designed to “put the blame for their upcoming defeat on someone else” – touching upon the much-talked about “Delhi vs Lucknow” faultlines in BJP. Indulging the sloganeering crowd, Rahul said his predictions always come true, and he was now forecasting that CEC Kumar would go to jail.“Vote chori” is no smalltime shoplifting but a “rarest of rare case” which qualifies as “treason”, Rahul said. “Without Gyanesh, Modi would not be PM and Shah would not be HM. He also accused RSS of capturing all institutions, including judiciary and bureaucracy, while “two or three people like Ambani and Adani have cornered all the wealth”. He said RSSBJP have spread hatred in the country and the opposition wants to restore “mohabbat ki dukaan” and a culture of nonviolence.“...The voice of every citizen of India is more important to me...” he said. NC’s Abdullah said BJPRSS call Muslims Pakistanis, but Muslims have worked to strengthen the country. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Survivors of the 1984 anti-Sikh killings and Sikh organisations Sunday questioned Congress's decision to hold the INDIA bloc rally on Nov 1, the 42nd anniversary of the massacre. With Punjab assembly elections due in 2027, the rally's timing also gave BJP political ammunition against Congress.The day saw a BJP-organised protest march in West Delhi, objections from victims' groups and renewed demands for justice.In West Delhi, Sikh community members and survivors joined a march from Hari Nagar towards Tilak Nagar, demanding an apology from Congress and Rahul Gandhi. Union minister Hardeep Singh Puri, Delhi CM Rekha Gupta, minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa and senior advocate HS Phoolka, who has represented riot victims for decades, participated."Nov 1 is not only a black day for the Sikhs but the entire country. They (Congress) should also observe it as a black day and hang their heads in shame," Phoolka had said ahead of the rally.The 1984 Riot Victims Welfare Society also objected to the timing of the rally. Its representatives, who had met Punjab governor Gulab Chand Kataria on Friday, said Nov 1 was a day of mourning, not political mobilisation. They also raised pending demands for housing, employment and rehabilitation.Society president Surjit Singh sought dignified rehabilitation, while women's wing president Bibi Gurdeep Kaur recalled losing eight family members in the violence.Rajya Sabha MP Vikramjit Singh Sahney, who met survivors in Delhi, recalled losing four family members and alleged that the killings were systematically planned.Separately, SGPC president Harjinder Singh Dhami described the massacre as "a stain on the forehead of the world's largest democracy". articles.title: Poverty removal not just slogan: PM Modi on World Bank data
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India has recorded one of the fastest poverty declines in the world, with the extreme poverty rate in the country \"collapsing\" by 90% between
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India has recorded one of the fastest poverty declines in the world, with the extreme poverty rate in the country "collapsing" by 90% between 2011 and 2023 to a low of 2.6%, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said on Saturday, while asserting that elimination of poverty is a commitment for his govt."A historic fall in poverty. A generational rise in opportunity... Gareebi hatao was never a slogan for us. It is our commitment. From more than 1 in 4 Indians to roughly 1 in 38 (in extreme poverty)," the PM posted on Instagram Saturday, citing the World Bank's latest numbers. He highlighted that nearly 50 crore people had moved out of poverty during these 12 years.Besides, Modi added, employment had grown by 13.4 crore between 2017 and 2023, which was nearly twice the increase in India's working age population. "Inequality has fallen sharply. India's Gini index has dropped by over 20% from 29 in 2011 to 23 in 2023," the Prime Minister said in the Instagram post. The Gini index reflects how equitable is the distribution of income or wealth across a population, with a lower number indicating greater equality.World Bank's latest Poverty and Equity brief, released last week, said that poverty rate in India, defined at $4.2 a day, will decline to 12.1% in 2028 from 57.7% in 2011, having fallen to 16.1% in 2023. Meanwhile, extreme poverty, defined as spending $3 a day, declined from 27.1% in 2011 to 2.6% in 2023."This progress was mainly driven by strong consumption growth; rising employment, especially among women; and expanded social transfers, including food subsidies. As poverty declined, it became increasingly concentrated among households with lower education, fewer assets, limited access to stable employment and higher dependency ratios. Wage disparities, however, remain pronounced, as median earnings among the top 10% of workers were about 13 times those of the bottom 10% in 2023," the World Bank had said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Nine killed in fiery Florida jet crash in West Palm Beach County
articles.summary: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy described the crash, which happened near President Trump's Mar-a-Lago resort, as a "horrific tragedy".
articles.body:
A business jet crashed in a neighbourhood in Florida on Sunday, killing all nine people on board, the US transport secretary has said.

The crash happened near the neighbourhood of Cresthaven, some nine miles (14 km) from Mar-a-Lago, President Donald Trump's resort in the wealthy enclave of Palm Beach County, around 12:50 EST (17:50 GMT).

Images from the crash show a crater-sized hole in a residential road, with patches of fire and pieces of concrete and debris from the Learjet 60 aircraft scattered.

The aircraft had departed from Austin, Texas, and was headed to the Bahamas, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said in a statement.

US media reports and flight analysis indicate that the jet was plummeting hundreds of feet per second before crashing.

Unverified footage posted on social media shows what appears to be a dash-camera recording the moment of the crash. It shows vehicles driving on a residential suburban street, when suddenly an aircraft nosedives into the ground almost vertically, and explodes into a large fireball.

"When you see that video, it's a jarring thing," Florida Governor Ron DeSantis told reporters at a news conference after the crash. "It's like a missile coming down, and a massive explosion, debris going everywhere."

It is not yet clear who was aboard the jet when it crashed. DeSantis said "as of now, we don't have any reports of anyone who was on the ground...who was killed or injured".

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy described the crash as a "horrific tragedy", and said the FAA was sending a team to the scene to help an investigation by the National Transportation Safety Board.

"Please join me in praying for the families and loved ones of those we lost," Duffy added.

Palm Beach County Fire Rescue has declared a "mass casualty incident".

The Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office said the crash happened on Military Trail, a six-lane road that features businesses and eateries.

At a news conference, DeSantis and local officials said that 600 local residents were being evacuated from a nearby trailer-park community.

The impact of the crash caused considerable damage to local infrastructure, including its water lines, they said, and it would be at least 30 days before the road re-opened.

Thunderstorms had been reported in the area at the time of the crash, and it was heavily raining as the news conference was held.

Trump had been at Mar-a-Lago on Sunday morning, and departed from an airport nearby on Air Force One about an hour before the crash.

articles.title: In 1937, Texas artist Buck Winn bought 1,164 acres in Hill Country; his descendants have now protected 165 acres permanently beside the Blanco River, preserving rare bird habitat, historic fences and two miles of creek
articles.summary: A historic ranch in Texas, once home to a celebrated regional artist, is continuing its legacy through a conservation effort led by his descendants.
articles.body: A historic ranch in Texas, once home to a celebrated regional artist, is continuing its legacy through a conservation effort led by his descendants. Four Winns Ranch, located near Wimberley in Hays County, has 165 acres protected permanently through a conservation easement, safeguarding its wildlife habitats, historic features and important water resources. According to a recent story published by the US Department of Agriculture's Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS) on October 29, 2026, the initiative was undertaken by the Winn family in partnership with Hill Country Conservancy. The property has a history stretching back several generations. James Buchanan Buck Winn Jr., a prominent Texas artist, purchased the original 1,164-acre property in 1937. He used the landscape as a family home and a source of inspiration for his creative work. His descendants have since continued their connection with the land by ensuring that a portion of the original ranch remains protected from future development. The conservation effort was also documented by the Land Trust Alliance in a 2020 case study on the Agricultural Conservation Easement Program.A ranch with an artistic and cultural legacyWinn was much more than a painter. He was a sculptor, inventor, architect, professor and pilot whose contributions to Texas' cultural landscape remain visible today. One of his best-known creations was The History of Ranching, a 280-foot mural originally displayed at San Antonio's Pearl Brewery. Parts of the work are now exhibited at institutions including the Wimberley Community Center and Texas State University. He also contributed murals to the Hall of State in Dallas for the 1936 Texas Centennial celebrations and created Morning Glories, a prominent feature at Aquarena Springs.The ranch itself carries a history that predates Winn's ownership. The landscape was once used by Indigenous communities who depended on its natural resources, including water and wildlife. Spanish presence followed during the 17th and 18th centuries, before Anglo settlers began moving into the region after Texas gained independence from Mexico in 1836.Among the property's surviving historical features are extensive stone fences believed to date back to around 1850. Running along the northern bank of Pierce Creek, these structures offer clues about the German settlers who established homesteads in the area.Rare bird species find refuge on the propertyBeyond its cultural significance, Four Winns Ranch provides an increasingly important refuge for wildlife in the Texas Hill Country. The landscape includes open pastures, rolling hills, cedar thickets and scattered oak groves. These natural features support a variety of plant and animal species, while providing nesting grounds, food and water for wildlife.A survey of the property identified nine bird species listed by Texas as Species of Greatest Conservation Need. These include the Summer Tanager, Rufous-crowned Sparrow and Red-shouldered Hawk, alongside the federally protected Golden-cheeked Warbler. The presence of these species highlights the ecological importance of protecting relatively undisturbed habitats in a region facing pressures from land fragmentation, excessive grazing and expanding development.Why protecting the Blanco River mattersOne of the most significant aspects of the conservation effort is the property's location along the Blanco River. The ranch also includes approximately two miles of Pierce Creek, an important tributary of the river.The Blanco River plays a role in replenishing the Edwards and Middle Trinity aquifers, which are important sources of groundwater for Central Texas. Protecting the surrounding landscape helps maintain water quality and supports the natural systems that depend on these waterways.The river also contributes to the water resources feeding popular natural destinations, including San Marcos Springs and Barton Springs. According to the NRCS, the Blanco River accounts for as much as 6% of the average recharge reaching Barton Springs. During drought conditions, it can become the only source of natural surface-water recharge. These water systems also support several endangered aquatic species, including the fountain darter, Texas blind salamander and Barton Springs salamander.A conservation agreement that allows the ranch to remain activeThe permanent conservation easement is held by Hill Country Conservancy in partnership with the NRCS through its Agricultural Conservation Easement Program's Agricultural Land Easement component (ACEP-ALE). The programme works with landowners and conservation organisations to prevent working agricultural properties from being converted into non-agricultural developments, including housing projects and commercial establishments.Importantly, protecting the property does not mean shutting it off from economic activity. The easement allows agricultural operations and ecotourism activities to continue. The ranch also hosts a zipline attraction that brings thousands of visitors across its hills and creeks each year. By combining conservation with continued use of the land, the Winn family's decision seeks to preserve the property's ecological and historical character while allowing future generations to remain connected to it.You use AI every day. articles.title: Introspect on need to improve judiciary responsiveness: CJI
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Flagging the importance of timely intervention by courts in crucial matters, CJI Surya Kant said the difference between justice and injustice
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Flagging the importance of timely intervention by courts in crucial matters, CJI Surya Kant said the difference between justice and injustice was not in the final judgement but in whether the court intervened when "intervention was most needed".He underlined the need for the judiciary, particularly constitutional courts, to introspect to further improve their working and to make listing of cases "more transparent and predictable".Speaking at the platinum jubilee celebration of Kerala HC, CJI Kant said constitutional justice in India did not begin and end in New Delhi and its strength lay in the robust network of 25 HCs spread across the country, each entrusted with the duty of protecting rights and upholding the rule of law.He said HCs were better placed to deal with citizens' problems as they were closely connected with the everyday realities of people."It is in this context that I wish to emphasise the extraordinary constitutional significance of Article 226. Its breadth is one of the greatest strengths of our judicial architecture. While Article 32 guarantees access to SC for enforcement of fundamental rights, Article 226 empowers HCs to issue appropriate writs and directions not only for fundamental rights but also for other legal rights. This wide constitutional canvas allows HCs to fashion meaningful remedies across diverse legal, statutory, administrative and contractual disputes. Equally important is their power to grant timely interim protection," the CJI said.He said there has been a growing tendency of litigants to approach SC requesting directions for urgent listing or early hearing of matters pending before HCs and asked whether the present process could be improved, including listing of cases."SC has consistently respected the institutional autonomy of HCs, including their authority to regulate their own rosters. That position is rooted in respect for the constitutional status of these institutions. Yet, the frequency of such requests invites us to consider whether there is room to improve the responsiveness of our processes. We must ask ourselves: Can urgent matters be identified more effectively? Can listing procedures be made more transparent and predictable? Can technology assist in prioritising cases where delay may cause irreversible prejudice?..." he said."These are not questions of institutional criticism but of collective responsibility," the CJI added.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Jesse Konig and Ben Johnson built a frozen French-fry brand around a seed-oil-free recipe; in 2026, Jesse & Ben’s raised $10 million to expand into Target and other major retailers
articles.summary: A frozen French-fry brand founded by two restaurant operators is taking its seed-oil-free approach to more supermarket shelves after securing $10 million
articles.body: A frozen French-fry brand founded by two restaurant operators is taking its seed-oil-free approach to more supermarket shelves after securing $10 million in Series A funding. Jesse Konig and Ben Johnson launched Jesse & Ben's in 2024, building its range around russet potatoes, grass-fed beef tallow and avocado oil. The brand has since expanded its retail presence, including a nationwide rollout at Target, and attracted investment from Greycroft and other backers. Announced on 7 May 2026, the funding is set to support production capacity, supply chain improvements, new product launches and further expansion across the US retail market.How two restaurant operators entered the frozen food businessJesse Konig and Ben Johnson came from the restaurant industry before turning their attention to packaged food. Their experience running food businesses gave them an understanding of what customers expected from restaurant-quality fries, but bringing that experience into supermarket freezers presented a different challenge.Jesse & Ben's co-founder outlines the next phase of growth:"When we started Jesse & Ben's, the goal was simple: turn junk food into joy food. Two years in, we're watching real people pick our bag over the brands they grew up with, and we're outselling legacy brands on shelves we never imagined we'd be on. This round gives us the firepower to keep launching products people actually want, to scale our supply chain, and to bring in the best operators in CPG. We couldn't have asked for a better group of partners to do it with."They introduced Jesse & Ben's to retail customers in June 2024. Rather than compete solely on convenience or price, the company built its products around a particular ingredient choice: avoiding seed oils. Its recipes use russet potatoes, grass-fed beef tallow or avocado oil, alongside seasonings.The founders wanted to offer familiar comfort food with a more limited ingredient list. The approach also gave the brand a clear identity in a frozen potato category dominated by established manufacturers and supermarket own-label products.What makes Jesse & Ben's frozen French fries differentThe company's original range included three varieties of restaurant-style fries. Potatoes form the base, while beef tallow and avocado oil are used as alternatives to the seed oils commonly found in many packaged fried foods.The use of 100% grass-fed beef tallow became a defining part of the brand's offering. Avocado oil provided another option for shoppers looking for a different cooking fat. The recipes were designed around relatively few ingredients rather than long lists of additives.Jesse & Ben's also described its approach as turning conventional snack and comfort foods into products with simpler formulations. Its founders used the phrase 'junk food into joy food' to explain the thinking behind the business.The company began extending its range in 2026. Sweet potato tallow fries, initially tested exclusively at Sprouts Farmers Market, were scheduled to reach more national retailers. Crinkle-cut beef tallow fries were also planned for selected stores during the summer.From Sprouts and Whole Foods to a nationwide Target launchRetail distribution played a large part in the company's early growth. Jesse & Ben's gained visibility through launches at Sprouts Farmers Market and Whole Foods Market, giving it access to shoppers already familiar with specialty and premium food products.The brand subsequently secured a nationwide rollout at Target. It also appeared in regional Costco rotations, while further retail launches were being developed. The pace of expansion was significant for a business that had only entered supermarket shelves in 2024. According to the company reported by PR Newswire, sales grew by more than 1,100% in 2025. It projected a further increase of between 300% and 400% in 2026.Jesse & Ben's also reported that its products had become the leading brand in the frozen potato category at several retailers, outperforming established competitors and private-label alternatives.Jesse & Ben's raises $10 million in Series A fundingOn 7 May 2026, Jesse & Ben's announced that it had closed a $10 million Series A funding round led by Greycroft. The investment was intended to support the next stage of the company's retail expansion as demand increased.Greycroft's involvement brought consumer investment experience to the business. Its partner Eric Ryan, who previously co-founded Method and Olly, was set to join Jesse & Ben's board. Brian Bustamante-Nicholson also backed the investment on behalf of the firm.Rich Products Ventures joined the round as a new investor. Existing backers included Willow Growth Partners, Sling Ventures, Midnight Venture Partners and grt sht ventures.The financing also attracted several entrepreneurs and consumer business figures. Among them were Andrew Abraham of Orgain, Carter Comstock of Freshly, Poppi co-founders Allison and Stephen Ellsworth, Sweetgreen co-founder Nic Jammet and Jordan Brown of Hu Chocolate. Creator-investors Lauryn and Michael Bosstick of Dear Media and The Skinny Confidential also participated.Where the new funding will goA large share of the $10 million was earmarked for production and supply chain improvements. With the brand entering more supermarket chains, maintaining enough stock to meet demand became a central part of its expansion plans.The money was also expected to support additional retail partnerships and recruitment. Moving from a relatively small operation into national distribution requires more than securing shelf space. Manufacturing capacity, logistics and a larger team all become necessary as order volumes increase.The company had already begun strengthening its management structure before announcing the financing. Audrey Burger, previously associated with Primal Kitchen and Kraft Heinz, joined as founding president. Jesse & Ben's also brought in other employees with experience at established food businesses, including Siete.New products as the brand expands its supermarket presenceThe planned product launches were another part of the company's growth strategy. Sweet potato tallow fries expanded on the original potato range, using sweet potatoes, grass-fed beef tallow and sea salt. The product was expected to move beyond its initial Sprouts test into additional national retail outlets.Crinkle-cut beef tallow fries were also due to join the core selection at selected retailers in summer 2026. The company was looking to extend its range while retaining the ingredient approach that had helped distinguish its first products.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Air Marshal Inderpal Singh Walia on Sunday assumed the appointment of Vice Chief of the Air Staff (VCAS) of the Indian Air Force.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Air Marshal Inderpal Singh Walia on Sunday assumed the appointment of Vice Chief of the Air Staff (VCAS) of the Indian Air Force. He took over from Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, who now has assumed charge as 29th IAF chief.On Sunday, he paid homage at the National War Memorial and was presented a ceremonial Guard of Honour.He was earlier Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief of Eastern Air Command. In a career spanning almost four decades, the Air Officer has tenanted various command and staff appointments. He has commanded a frontline fighter squadron, the Tactics and Air Combat Development Establishment (TACDE) and was Air Officer Commanding of Air Force Station Bareilly. He is qualified on all variants of MiG-21, MiG-23, MiG-27, Jaguar and Su-30 MKI.He had undergone Advanced Command & Staff Course in the UK and NDC in Bangladesh, headed Directorate of Air Staff Inspection (DASI) of the IAF, served as a defence attache at the Embassy of Japan and South Korea, and was the Senior Air Staff Officer of Eastern Air Command.Walia is an alumnus of the National Defence Academy and was commissioned in the fighter stream of the IAF on June 11, 1988. He is an avid reader and holds three postgraduate degrees in Defence and Strategic Studies. In recognition of distinguished service, he was awarded the Vayu Sena Medal (VM) in 2008 and Ati Vishisht Seva Medal (AVSM) in 2018.

articles.summary: This Monday, despite the forceful nature of Scorpio’s ruler, the wiser course of action is to adopt a more leisurely attitude.
articles.body: This Monday, despite the forceful nature of Scorpio’s ruler, the wiser course of action is to adopt a more leisurely attitude. Mars, which is debilitated in Cancer, occupies the ninth house and is now moving through Ashlesha nakshatra, with its deep, coiled energy. Moreover, the Moon also dwells there today. This might give rise to the impulse to solve everything right away. Yet Shani, retrograde in Pisces in your fifth house, in Uttara Bhadrapada, advises rest before taking any action.Ashlesha Turns Energy InwardAshlesha shrouds energy inward. Because Mars, your ruler, is weak, you may experience bursts of energy, followed by low spirits.You may feel tempted to finish a pile of tasks or sort out that troublesome family situation. Most of the activities can wait till mid-week.Advice Comes from ShaniShani occupying the fifth house is in harmony with the Moon and Mars in Cancer. A little relaxation after lunch can do more good than any hasty efforts tonight.Decisions taken after relaxation are more likely to stick.Plenty of Companions in the TwelfthIn light of the current situation, it makes sense to maintain light evening plans.Jupiter Keeps the TenthJupiter in Leo, your tenth house, will protect important professional opportunities even if you decide to take it slow.Do’s for TodayRest after lunch.Postpone non-urgent actions until mid-week.Don’ts for TodayDo not try to clear everything in a rush.Do not make any decisions when feeling exhausted.Shani Remedy for the DayThis week, give a worker or domestic helper a paid day off.On Monday evening, offer red flowers to Lord Kartikeya.Get the latest astrology news and horoscope updates.
